sentence_of_record: STAGE3-MATH-CAPFREE (2026-09-16, 5,992 calls): FRAMEWORK item 23 on the admitted population: PASS, prediction held; the cheap judge with a checker reference reaches 0.96 on terminated MATH traces. With a checker (exact) reference and terminated traces the cheap judge's key-decidable accuracy is 0.958 against 0.849-0.852 on MMLU-Pro under a possibly-wrong reasoning reference and 0.935 on GEN-ARENA's unfiltered MATH cell: the reference ceiling, not the judge, is what MMLU-Pro measures (ORACLE's line). [RESTATED 2026-09-23 by the adversarial audit (insertion only; 0.958 and the PASS stand): the comparison in this clause is a POSITIONING, not a measurement. 0.958 is MATH / 8 models / checker output / terminated traces only (16.5% of question-pairs excluded, the exclusion selective on correctness: removed rows' key accuracy 0.034 vs 0.427) / n = 1,537 convention A; 0.849-0.852 is MMLU-Pro / 12 models / cached reasoning reference / n = 4,499-4,507 on the full x12 schedule. Different corpus, roster, reference form and population; the two were never judged on a shared match and BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT's does_not_show forbids reading such a step as a paired test. The only paired reference contrast inside one corpus in the whole record is PAIR-NOREF's 0.864 vs 0.738 on identical MMLU-Pro matches. AND the reading "the reference ceiling, not the judge, is what MMLU-Pro measures" is stronger than the row it cites: ORACLE's criterion (4) decomposes the residual as reference-induced error 0.165 against the judge's IRREDUCIBLE error 0.223 on 302 paired matches, and ORACLE's does_not_show records "a reference-only explanation of the residual (the judge's own error is the larger half)". The two sentences are in the record together and are not reconciled; see the OPEN CONTRADICTION note.] The cost of the cap is on the record beside it: 16.5% of question-pairs excluded, and per-model checker accuracy up to +0.10 higher on admitted rows.

plain_description.what: Measures the cheap judge's accuracy against the key on MATH, 8 models (5,992 calls). The judge gets an exact checker reference answer. Responses cut off by the 1,024-token generation cap are excluded (83.5% of question pairs kept).
plain_description.why: The unfiltered MATH cell failed the accuracy bar because truncated answers polluted it. The test asks whether the judge is reliable on the population the framework's rules admit.
plain_description.information: Passing shows the cheap judge is accurate when it has an exact reference. Result: done, passed (0.958 accuracy, bar 0.75). Comparing this with MMLU-Pro's 0.85 is only a positioning, not a measurement: corpus, models and reference type differ, and the excluded rows were mostly wrong answers. It says nothing about the truncated responses or about calibration.
